description: Sync deals, leads, projects, tasks, persons, organizations, activities and notes from one Pipedrive account. Pipedrive visibility settings are not enforced.
opening: Sync a whole Pipedrive account: deals, leads, projects and project tasks, persons, organizations, activities such as calls and meetings, and notes. Each record is one document. Stage, pipeline, organization, person, activity type, product and lead label ids are turned into names. A note or activity links to every deal, person, organization and lead it is attached to.

Pipedrive's visibility setting is kept as a filter but does not restrict who can read an item, so every synced item is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Records deleted in Pipedrive stay in HydraDB. Pipedrive mail, files and call logs are not synced.

notes: Pipedrive's `visible_to` setting is stored as `additional_metadata.visible_to`. You can filter on it, but it does not decide who can read an item.

connect.auth: Pipedrive uses a personal API token.

credentials.name: api_token
credentials.text: A Pipedrive personal API token. The connector reads every record this token can see.

steps.title: Copy an API token
steps.text: In Pipedrive, copy the personal API token of a user who can see the records you want in HydraDB.

steps.title: Configure the connector
steps.text: Pipelines are offered for selection, but selecting them does not narrow the sync. The connector syncs every record the token can read in the account.

connect.account: One connector reads one Pipedrive account.

sync.first_sync: Reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads records whose update time moved past the last sync. A deal's line items are read again whenever the deal changes.
sync.edits: An edited record is read again and updates its document.
sync.deletes: Deleted records are not removed. They stay searchable in HydraDB. A record Pipedrive marks as deleted is flagged, so you can leave it out with `additional_metadata.is_deleted`, or `additional_metadata.active_flag` for notes.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.pipedrive_id
shared_attributes.text: The Pipedrive record id. Ids can repeat across record types, so combine it with `additional_metadata.pipedrive_object` to target one record. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.pipedrive_object
shared_attributes.text: The record type, such as `deals`, `persons` or `notes`. Limits a query to one type. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

documents.name: Deals
documents.title: The deal title.
documents.text: The deal title, then `Value` with its currency, `Status`, `Lost reason`, `Stage`, `Pipeline`, `Organization`, `Contact`, `Expected close` and `Owner` lines. Then a `Products` block listing each line item with its quantity, price, currency and comments. The deal's key and creation time are part of the text too.

example_searches: Which deals for Acme are open and at what stage?
What was discussed in the last call with this person?
Which deals include the Enterprise plan product?

connections: A note or activity to every deal, person, organization and lead it is attached to.
An activity to each person who took part.
A deal or lead to its organization and contact person.
A project to every linked deal, organization and person.
A task to its project and its parent task.
people: Owners of deals, leads, persons, organizations and activities appear in the text, where HydraDB can identify them.
Project owners and task assignees are kept with the item but not attached to it as people.
graph.from_text: Notes, activity notes, deal titles, and project and task descriptions, along with the rest of each record's text.

not_synced: Pipedrive mail messages and mail threads.
Files, call logs and deal stage-change history.
Project boards and phases, task audit users and lead marketing attribution.
Records removed from Pipedrive entirely: they stay in HydraDB.
